fixed_global_transition_model.name: EXPLICIT_STANDARD_LASSERRE_SUM_OF_SQUARES_LEVEL_ESCALATION
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: Encode the 3-CNF/k-CSP in the standard explicit Lasserre/SoS hierarchy and obtain exact negative authority only when a hierarchy level refutes feasibility; levels are increased within that explicit hierarchy.
fixed_global_transition_model.globality: The state uses global moment/consistency data and is not merely bounded-local clause propagation.
fixed_global_transition_model.standard_upper_bound_not_used_as_lower_b: The cited paper states that level r can be optimized in time n^{O(r)} for poly(n)-constraint k-CSPs. This is an upper bound only and is not used as a runtime lower bound.
fixed_global_transition_model.explicit_state_indexing: In the standard level-r formulation described by the cited paper, vectors are explicitly defined for AND functions on subsets of up to r variables. Hence the materialized state contains at least one indexed object for every subset I with |I| <= r.

published_theorem.author: Grant Schoenebeck
published_theorem.title: Linear Level Lasserre Lower Bounds for Certain k-CSPs
published_theorem.statement_used: For every k >= 3, even Omega(n) levels of the Lasserre hierarchy cannot disprove random k-CSP instances over predicate types implied by k-XOR, including k-SAT and k-XOR. Thus there is a constant alpha>0 such that, in the covered random regime, globally unsatisfiable 3-SAT instances survive through alpha*n hierarchy levels with high probability.
published_theorem.explicit_formulation_fact_used: The paper's level-r formulation can be represented by defining vectors for AND functions of up to r variables; this explicitly indexes at least all variable subsets of size at most r.
published_theorem.cost_statement_firewall: The n^{O(r)} optimization statement is recorded only as an upper bound and is never reversed into a lower bound.

elementary_state_lower_bound.statement: If r >= alpha*n for any fixed alpha>0, the explicit standard level-r state contains at least binomial(n, min(r, floor(n/2))) indexed subset objects, which is 2^{Omega(n)}.
proof: The explicit formulation contains at least one object for each subset I of variables with |I| <= r.
If 0 < alpha <= 1/2 and r >= alpha*n, it contains at least binomial(n, floor(alpha*n)) objects; by the standard entropy/Stirling bound this is 2^{Omega(n)}.
If alpha > 1/2, level r contains all floor(n/2)-subsets, at least binomial(n, floor(n/2)) = 2^{Omega(n)}/poly(n).
Therefore materializing the standard explicit hierarchy at any linear level has exponential state size.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: The explicit standard Lasserre/SoS level-escalation route cannot serve as a universal polynomial-state/polynomial-work exact TRUMP transition law for arbitrary 3-CNF.
reason: Schoenebeck supplies unsatisfiable random 3-SAT instances that survive a linear number alpha*n of Lasserre levels.
Thus this exact route cannot obtain negative authority before reaching beyond that linear-order level on those instances.
But the explicit standard level-alpha*n formulation already contains 2^{Omega(n)} indexed subset/vector objects.
Therefore this materialized route violates L4 polynomial live-state and consequently cannot satisfy L3 polynomial charged work when the full standard level is explicitly constructed/processed.
The failure is not bounded-local blindness: the hierarchy is global, but exactness requires a globally indexed state of exponential size in this fixed implementation model.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: A globally informed relaxation can still contain a semantic dead zone: pseudo-distributions/moment data remain feasible even when no Boolean assignment exists.

what_is_not_proved: No runtime lower bound is inferred from the paper's n^{O(r)} upper bound.
No lower bound is claimed for implicit implementations that do not materialize the standard level-r subset/vector state.
No lower bound is claimed for arbitrary semidefinite/global algorithms outside the fixed explicit standard Lasserre/SoS hierarchy route.
No lower bound is claimed for every individual 3-CNF instance.
The result does not prove that global information is insufficient in principle; it blocks this precise explicit global relaxation architecture as an easier universal route.

next_admissible_math.question: Can TRUMP specify a genuinely global exact transition whose state is represented implicitly or by a non-relaxation invariant of polynomial size, and prove that each update and total trajectory are polynomial without reducing to generic proof search, bounded-local propagation, full-function compilation, or explicit linear-level Lasserre/SoS?
forbidden: reversing algorithmic upper bounds into lower bounds
materializing exponential hierarchy state while calling the macrostep polynomial
renaming known proof/relaxation machines without changing their mathematical semantics
